A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Riemannian MeanFlow work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments on spherical, toroidal, and SO(3) data, including MMD, NLL, conditional generation, dimensionality studies, and training throughput.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds grasp generation, promoter DNA generation, sampling-step comparisons, and capacity, limited-data, and memorization experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same transported average velocity, geodesic interpolation, JVP target, decomposed objective, PCGrad updates, and CFG formulation. The new applications and surrogate-error analysis do not document a changed algorithm or new method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds rigid-body grasp generation on SE(3), using the grasp dataset attributed to Eppner et al., and promoter DNA generation using FANTOM5 sequences of dimension 1024×4 (Sections 5.2–5.3). These substantially broaden task and domain coverage beyond the retained spherical, torsion-angle, rotation, and synthetic hypersphere experiments.

E2.justification: The new DNA comparison in v2 Table 7 includes Dirichlet FM, Fisher FM, and Woo et al.'s Eulerian, Lagrangian, and Semigroup RMF variants. None was a reported experimental comparator in v1; Woo et al. appeared only in the research discussion. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include grasp success at 1–7 steps, DNA MSE and k-mer correlation, spherical KLD, and sampling sweeps from 1 to 128 steps. Tables 15–17 add reduced model sizes, 100%/10%/1% training-data conditions, and leave-one-out nearest-neighbor comparisons. The existing 8/1/1 split and original hyperparameter settings remain stated as before.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 7 adds sampling-step sensitivity analysis. Tables 15–17 investigate capacity reduction, performance with limited training data, and possible memorization through train-generated versus test-generated nearest-neighbor comparisons. These substantially extend the retained gradient-conflict, CFG, and hypersphere analyses.

E5.justification: v2 adds formal MMD permutation testing across datasets and training-data fractions (Appendix G, Table 16), specifying 1000 generated versus 1000 held-out samples, 100 permutations, and a minimum reported p-value resolution of 0.01. The existing five-seed means and NLL standard deviations are retained; no increase in repeated-run counts is reported.

E6.justification: Matched pre-existing numerical results are unchanged, but substantial new results appear. Table 4 reports one-step grasp success of 65% for RMF, 60% for G-LSD, and 3.2% for RFM; Table 7 reports RMF DNA MSE 0.030 and k-mer correlation 0.94. New KLD scores, sampling curves, and capacity/data-fraction results further expand the evidence.

T1.justification: New Appendix B introduces bounded-curvature, speed, and velocity assumptions, a normal-coordinate Christoffel estimate, and Proposition B.2 bounding surrogate error by C0 U K V²(t−r)². Appendix D.3 supplies its proof. This is a substantive theoretical addition beyond v1's retained identity, loss decomposition, and geodesic derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion extend the claimed empirical scope to SE(3) robotic grasping. The central contributions—intrinsic average-velocity modeling, practical tangent-space supervision, conflict-aware optimization, and CFG—retain their previous meaning.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly explains that the practical JVP surrogate omits a connection correction and may incur greater error for high curvature or long transport intervals. The SE(3) discussion distinguishes distribution fitting from physical grasp feasibility, while Appendix G interprets capacity and limited-data findings as lacking a consistent memorization signature and explains the omitted torus nearest-neighbor diagnostic.

D1.justification: New Tables 13–14 disclose parameter counts and dataset scales, including 50K training samples per hypersphere setting and 732K–860K parameters. The original hyperparameter values remain unchanged in renumbered Tables 18–19. Conversely, explicit NOAA and EOSDIS data-source URLs present in v1's references are removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Brewin, Eppner et al., Hon et al., Fisher Flow Matching, and Dirichlet Flow Matching for the new theory and applications. Section 4's positioning against GFM, alpha-Flow, and Woo et al. is largely retained. Publication metadata updates for existing references do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: v2 expands the probability-path background and experimental discussion, inserts the curvature-analysis appendix and proof subsection, and makes localized wording and heading corrections. It also adds acknowledgments and changes the publication footer. The main narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: New Tables 4, 7, and 12–17 add application comparisons, KLD, capacity disclosures, and statistical diagnostics; new Figure 7 provides a substantial multipanel sampling-step comparison. Existing figures are retained and repositioned or renumbered, and the two hyperparameter tables are brought together on the final page.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the paper's efficiency and applicability claims: Figure 7 directly tests sampling-budget tradeoffs, Tables 15–17 examine capacity and limited-data behavior, and the grasp and DNA experiments extend practical validation. Appendix B also makes the surrogate's local approximation limits explicit, addressing an important qualification missing from v1. Detailed configurations for the new applications remain sparse, but the broader validation and clearer limitations provide a substantial net quality improvement.
